🔥🇲🇽 <u>Anti-Corruption Prosecutors Sit on 94% of Cases</u>

Of 1,300 criminal complaints filed by Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry, only 80 have reached a judge. That leaves 93.9% stuck at the FGR's anti-corruption unit, headed since 2019 by María de la Luz Mijangos, reports Miguel Badillo in Contralínea. Ten months into Ernestina Godoy's term as Attorney General, the purge of prosecutors continues. Some cases sit so long that the crimes expire.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Sheinbaum Backs Banxico's Rate Cut: "When Rates Fall, Investors Think About Investing"</u>

Sheinbaum backed the Bank of Mexico's 25-basis-point cut and said Hacienda sees no problem for the economy or the peso. She told markets to respect the central bank's autonomy: "The Bank of Mexico doesn't make decisions on the opinion of three people. It's a huge institution with analysts who review each case." Her explanation of the cut: "When interest rates go down, the investor thinks more about investing their money than keeping it stashed away."

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court Chief Hugo Aguilar Brings Fine-Tuning of the Judicial Reform to Congress</u>

A year into Mexico's first elected judiciary, Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar handed Ricardo Monreal and Raúl Bolaños a proposal to adjust the 2024 reform: budgetary autonomy for each judicial body, a plenary of the heads of the federal judiciary's top bodies, and the option for the Court to split into two chambers when caseloads pile up. The financial-independence piece already passed the Budget Commission in the 2027 spending plan. The court the pundits said would collapse is now asking for room to work faster.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE Lights Up 99.92% of Mexico — Well Above the World Average</u>

Mexico's state utility CFE closed September with 99.92% electricity coverage, versus a global average of 91.9% per the World Bank. Through October it finished 5,635 electrification works for 2,207 million pesos, bringing power to more than 140,000 people in remote communities the private market never bothered with. Next target, set by Sheinbaum: 99.99% by 2028.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Keeps Only 30 Cents of Every Tech Export Dollar</u>

Mexico supplies about 40% of US server imports. But of every dollar of electronics it exports, only 30 cents stay in the country, versus close to 50 cents in autos, IIF senior economist Jonathan Fortun told El Economista. The gap is imported inputs: most of the components come from abroad, which limits the value added at home.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>Energy Regulator Approves Six Solar Plants: $750 Million, 649 MW</u>

Mexico's National Energy Commission (CNE) approved six solar projects worth about $750 million. They add 649 MW of net capacity and 1,881 GWh a year, all with battery storage. Of 57 applications in the second call, 31 qualified for a generation permit, but only six met every criterion. 37% of the capacity comes online in 2028 and the rest in 2029.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS Takes Over Ecatepec's Children's Cancer Hospital, Unfinished Since 2014</u>

The Pediatric Oncology Hospital in Ecatepec has sat in raw concrete for more than 12 years. Sheinbaum said IMSS will finish it and asked director Zoé Robledo to present the plan along with a history of the abandonment. Her target was the right that still defends Seguro Popular, a system that left more than 80 hospitals abandoned while states bought medicines from a handful of firms charging up to triple. Today IMSS-Bienestar care is free in 24 states, including every cancer drug. Quoting Monsiváis on the right: "Its ideology is hypocrisy."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Has Eliminated 88% of Its Ozone-Depleting HCFCs</u>

At the Montreal Protocol meeting in Kigali (MOP38, Nov 2–6), Semarnat undersecretary Ileana Villalobos reported that Mexico has cut its consumption of hydrochlorofluorocarbons 88% from its national baseline as of December 2025, with total elimination set for 2030. Since 2024 Mexico has run import quotas on HFCs under the Kigali Amendment, and in 2025 it finished converting its commercial refrigeration manufacturing to lower-impact alternatives.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>6,000 Paisano Vehicles Expected Through Nuevo Laredo for the Holidays</u>

Mexico's consulate in Laredo, Texas, is already preparing the December caravan: about 6,000 vehicles of Mexicans coming home from the US, matching last year. Registration is Dec 15 and the convoy leaves Dec 16 at 4 a.m., coordinated by the consulate, customs, migration and police. "Those who come to Mexico need certainty of security in their transit," said Consul Juan Carlos Mendoza Sánchez.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum Asks Immigration to Confirm Taddei and the Hernández Casillas Brothers Are Still in Mexico</u>

Rumors placed former INE chief Guadalupe Taddei in the US and INE contractors José Alfredo and Raymundo Hernández Casillas in South America. "Yes, it seems so," Sheinbaum said Friday when asked whether they remain in Mexico, but she asked the National Migration Institute (INM) for a formal report. On Lorenzo Córdova, who admitted he knew the firms existed: "Why didn't he do anything? And why did they contract more than 2 billion pesos?"
banner: TADDEI: INM ASKED TO CONFIRM WHEREABOUTS
